assessments.task: Compare expiration to peak inspiration and point out the descending diaphragm dome, descending lung bases and liver shift.

axes.observation: The exact assembly, sampled at frames 1 and 49, shows the upper diaphragm bound descending 20.90 mm, the left lower-lobe base descending 17.60 mm and the liver descending 7.98 mm. At frame 121 these bounds return within 0.034 mm of frame 1. The motion is authored.

Matched neutral lateral close-ups show the broad diaphragm highlight moving down toward its open rim as the lung bases descend. The irregular lower-lobe edges are retained Workshop surfaces. At peak the projected basal edge overlaps the lateral rim, so the image cannot establish contact or attachments.

The retained phase pair shows lower lung edges and a downward liver shift. The liver occludes part of the dome, and the apex shift is subtle at full view. An isolated side view is needed for learners to follow flattening.

The exact assembly has 245,126 source mesh triangles in 67 selectable meshes and 69 exact-position connected pieces, with 183 transform F-curves and six morph F-curves. Only 93,502 triangles belong to the five lobes, diaphragm and liver used for this task. Neighboring moving organs have broader teaching uses but add 151,624 triangles outside this view. No same-scope lighter editable assembly has been compared.
